Subject: Dedicated sizing question for Mistral workload

Hi Camila,

Quick note — we’re sizing a pilot for Nimbus that will run a real-time chat assistant (Mistral-13B family). Expected profile: median user prompt ~60 tokens, median assistant response ~220 tokens (so ~280 tokens/request). Peak concurrency we expect during US daytime is ~100–140 RPS (we're planning around 120 RPS as a realistic peak). The p95 latency target we need to meet is <= 350ms for the interactive product.

Questions:
- Can Redwood map token/sec to GPU counts for this model / quantization we discussed?
- What safety headroom would you recommend for a committed slab vs burst?
- Any fallback model suggestions if we need to reduce latency during spikes?

We’re also working with procurement so ballpark committed monthly commit guidance would be helpful.

Thanks — Sam
Sam Li
Head of Product, Nimbus AI

Sam — thanks for the clear profile. I ran a quick top-line before we do a formal calc. Attaching a short draft (mistral_capacity_draft_v1.pdf) and a small KV cache warm-up worksheet. High level:

- Baseline math uses your 280 tokens/request at 120 RPS => ~33,600 tokens/sec sustained at peak.
- For Mistral-13B quantized (int8-ish/AMPQ profile) our runtime sees ~1.2k–1.5k tokens/sec/GPU at low-latency config (single-stream, optimized kernels) — depends on sequence-length and key-value cache hit rates.
- That implies ~24–28 GPUs to meet peak tokens/sec without headroom.

I’m looping in Karthik to formalize the GPU count with latency tail modeling (p95). Also CC’ing Ben for committed slab/contracting guidance.

Next steps: Karthik will share two scenarios (conservative and aggressive) with headroom and suggested burst sizing; Ben will advise commit tiers and recommended contract.

— Camila
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodai.com

Folks — I took Camila’s baseline and did a short SLO fit exercise. Key assumptions up-front:
- Model: Mistral-13B, quantized to int8-ish profile (we’ll call this Q8 MVC).
- Typical request tokens: 280 total; average autoregressive step distribution approximated by your median/95th breakdown; we assume most requests are < 512 total tokens.
- Hardware: A100-style GPU performance table (normalized). For Q8 Mistral-13B: ~1,350 tokens/sec/GPU at single-stream low-latency with KV caching warmed. For Mistral-7B Q8: ~3,000 tokens/sec/GPU.

Scenario A — Conservative (SLO-first)
- Peak token/sec required: 120 RPS * 280 = 33,600 tps.
- Map to GPUs (base): 33,600 / 1,350 ≈ 25 GPUs.
- Add SLO headroom (p95 tail, request concurrency variance, node-level failures): multiplier 1.6 => recommend reserved slab = 40 GPUs.
- Burst buffer: allow autoscale to +50% (i.e., up to 60 GPUs) for short spikes; route lower-critical traffic to fallback model during scale-up.
- Expected p95 under this config: ~320–360ms depending on KV hit-rate (higher hit-rate => lower latency).

Scenario B — Cost-balanced (Commit + Model fallback)
- Reserve a smaller slab for cost: 28 GPUs (near-base coverage) with aggressive burst to 48 GPUs during peak.
- Implement model fallback policy: a) if slab utilization > 85% for 3+ minutes, route 30% of low-priority requests to Mistral-7B (Q8), b) keep high-priority requests on 13B.
- With this hybrid, effective tokens/sec capacity = (28 * 1,350) + (0.3 * traffic * 3,000) ≈ handles 33,600 with p95 drift to ~380–420ms during sustained spikes.

Operational notes:
- KV cache warm-up: cold-starts can double latency; recommend warm-up buckets + prefix caching for first 10 minutes of known events. See attached kv-cache-warmup-plan.xlsx.
- Quantization testing: QA with your prompt distribution; some prompts (long chains) regress quality on 7B fallback.
- Rollout suggestion: start with Scenario B for first 30 days, monitor % of routed fallback and latency; convert to Scenario A if SLA violations > 0.5% at p95.

I’ll drop a simple GPU mapping table and a token-runway calculator to the Drive link Camila shared.

— Karthik
Principal Infra SRE, Redwood Inference

Sam — quick commercial readout to match Karthik’s scenarios:

- Scenario A (40 reserved GPUs) — recommended for product teams that require strong p95 guarantees. Ballpark monthly commit: equivalent to 40 x reserved-GPU-month. We’d price this as a Dedicated slab with 12-month minimum; discount tiers apply at 36+ GPU-months. I’ll prepare a formal quote, but expect an uplift vs Scenario B of ~30% in monthly cost for the additional headroom.

- Scenario B (28 reserved + burst to 48 + fallback) — lower upfront commit, faster time-to-launch. For procurement: propose a 6–12 month commit window with a burst pool and an overage pricing slab. This is our standard mid-tier enterprise pattern.

Recommended next steps:
1) Camila/Engineering to finalize the capacity draft and confirm fallback quality expectations (by EOD Friday).
2) Ben to issue a two-option commercial term sheet (Scenario A vs Scenario B) and include DocuSign link.
3) Karthik to provide the small token-runway CSV and latency-vs-headroom table shared to the Drive.

I’ll queue a pricing draft and the DocuSign for signatures — Sam, let us know which scenario you prefer and we’ll convert to a formal PO workflow.
